Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

minor adjective

small, of little importance

also trivial, trifling, unimportant, petty, slight, a minor matter, of no importance, secondary, of secondary importance

classical

Cic. Sen. 63: quae videntur levia atque commūnia
Cic. Deiot. 5: leviōra (Lewis & Short)

levis, leve

adjective, third declension

slight, trifling, of little weight

First “light in weight” (against gravis); figuratively “of no weight”, unimportant, trivial, and of persons fickle, unreliable (Lewis & Short). Not to be confused with lēvis, “smooth”, with a long e.

Other words

  • nūllīus mōmentī — of no importance

    phrase: genitive of quality; also parvī mōmentī, magnī mōmentī · also used · classical · Cic. Vatin. 1: nūllīus mōmentī aliquid putāre (Lewis & Short); Caes. BG 7.39: levī mōmentō aestimāre (Lewis & Short)

    Mōmentum is the weight that tips a balance; so a thing of no, little or great moment. See important.

  • minor, minus — smaller, lesser; of less account

    adjective, comparative of parvus, declension · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 2.214: sunt nōtitiā multa minōra tuā (Lewis & Short, s.v. parvus)

    A true comparative, “smaller, less”: of age, younger (minor nātū, see younger); of rank, inferior. “Too trivial for” is minor with the ablative, as in Ovid. English “minor” as a plain adjective is usually levis or parvus (see small).

Examples

  • haec enim ipsa sunt honōrābilia quae videntur levia atque commūnia

    for these very things, which seem slight and ordinary, are marks of honourCic. Sen. 63

See also important, small, minor, younger, serious.
